newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Royal Sun integration on course.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Royal Sun integration on course.

text.p: British insurer Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc said on Thursday it was on target to deliver the 175 million pounds ($280.2 million) of annualised savings promised at the time the time of last year's six billion pound merger.
Around 3,000 jobs have already gone and savings are currently running at some 95 million pounds.
The grouop reported an 11 percent rise in first half profits to 501 million pounds, marking the end of the first year of merged operations.
The strong pound, a major feature of the company reporting season so far, took some 25 million pounds off the headline figure.
In morning trading, shares in Royal Sun added 18 pence to 540-1/2 pence.
Many analysts have suggested the benefits of the merger could eventually exceed expectations, but chief executive Richard Gamble refused to be drawn.
He said the company was looking to reduce costs across all parts of its business and it was dificult to say what additional savings were merger benefits.
The results topped market expectations and Gamble picked out the UK and U.S. performances.
In Britain, the group had spent a long time focusing on the core skills of underwriting and claims management both of which were prime features of the group's first half performance, he said.
However, the UK rating environment remains difficult and profits slipped slightly to 165 million pounds from 172 million pounds last year.
Personal motor insurance was the only area seeing a rise in rates and Royal Sun has put through increases of 10 percent in the last twelve months.
That has had a knock-on effect on exposures which are down seven percent year-on-year but the company said it was prepared to let non-profitable business go.

Like Commercial Union, which reported on Wednesday, costs from property subsidence were up. They increased by 19 million pounds to 56 million pounds, mainly as a result of the dry period between January and April.
General insurance profits worldwide rose 22 million pounds to 374 million pounds helped by an excellent performance in the U.S. and Canada.
U.S. profits rose 44 million pounds to 92 million pounds partly reflecting lower weather and catstrophe costs.
Now a top ten operator in UK life business, Gamble said Royal Sun intended to be a major player but was cautious about acquisitions.
European life companies were 'extravagantly expensive', he said, and it was difficult to justify an acquisition benefiting shareholders.
He refused to rule one out completely but said the focus was very much on completing the integration.
Over the six months worldwide life profits climbed 16 percent to 108 million pounds.

Royal Sun reaffirmed its commitment to active management of its capital base but Gamble said a number of factors needed to be taken into account when weighing up the possibility of further share buybacks.
The company has already embarked on a repurchase of five percent of its shares. To date it has bought back some 32 million shares, less than half the amount planned.
A major factor underlying the group's solvency figures was booming stockmarkets around the world and the question of whether that would continue had to be taken into account, said Gamble.

Responding to Wednesday's remarks from Britain's Personal Investment Authority (PIA) that the company had failed to meet the first deadline set in its pension misselling review Gamble insisted that it had delivered what it promised.
He declined to give a figure for the provisions set aside to meet the costs of the pensions misselling.

The half year dividend was raised 10 percent to 7.15 pence per share and the net asset value per share increased to 433 pence from 399 pence. As of August 4 it had risen further to 455 pence. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
